title: Discovery of a [C I]-faint, CO-bright Galaxy: ALMA Observations of the Merging Galaxy NGC 6052
question: Why is [C I](1-0) undetected relative to CO(4-3) in the merging galaxy NGC 6052, and can [C I] trace its molecular gas mass?

data.sensitivity: rms 61.5 mJy/beam ([C I]) and 46.8 mJy/beam (CO 4-3) at 15 km/s

what.value: CO(1-0) flux, IRAM 30m (16.4 K km/s in 24'' beam)

evidence.quote: from the integrated intensity reported as 16.4 [K km s$^{-1}$] in the 24$''$ single-dish beam

what.value: SPIRE/FTS line fluxes and U/LIRG comparison sample

evidence.quote: together with the data for nearby U/LIRGs observed by SPIRE/FTS (cite: Kame_2016)
The flux of [O I]$_{63}$ and [C II]$_{158}$ is 82 and 138 [W m$^{-1}$] (cite: Diaz-Santos_2017)

recipe.method: tclean with Briggs weighting at 15 km/s resolution

recipe.goal: Measure CO(4-3) flux and [C I] upper limit
recipe.method: Integrate primary-beam-corrected spectrum over FoV; 3 sigma upper limit for [C I] using box/beam scaling
key_parameters: FWHM=96 km/s assumed for [C I]; N_box=3990; N_beam=247
assumptions: [C I] line shape same as CO(4-3)

recipe.method: L (Lsun) and L' (K km/s pc^2) equations from Solomon & Vanden Bout
